title: Sprite::AddDisplayObject detour declares 4 of the function's 9 parameters; the 5 stack args (incl. CharacterCreateInfo* and InteractiveObject* parent) are not forwarded
our_code: src/goblin_gfx_probe.cpp:54 (using AddDispFn = void *(void *, void *, void *, void *)), src/goblin_gfx_probe.cpp:440 (adddisp_detour), installed src/goblin_gfx_probe.cpp:2158
claim: We assume the function at RVA 0x0F01B10 takes 4 arguments (rcx,rdx,r8,r9) and forward exactly those to the trampoline. It actually takes `this` + 8 parameters: four in registers and FIVE on the stack, and it reads every one of them. Our detour's own frame supplies whatever happens to be at [rsp+0x28..0x48] when it calls the trampoline, so arg5..arg9 are garbage unless MSVC happens to emit a tail-jmp (which it cannot do on the `g_ms_watch_cid` path at goblin_gfx_probe.cpp:498, where the trampoline result is used before returning).
evidence:
SDK mangled name (authoritative): C:\Program Files (x86)\Scaleform\GFx SDK 4.0\Lib\x64\Msvc90\Release\libgfx.lib contains `?AddDisplayObject@Sprite@GFx@Scaleform@@UEAAPEAVDisplayObjectBase@23@AEBVCharPosInfo@23@AEBVASString@23@PEBV?$ArrayLH@PEAVSwfEvent@GFx@Scaleform@@$0BAE@UArrayDefaultPolicy@3@@3@PEBXIKPEAUCharacterCreateInfo@23@PEAVInteractiveObject@23@@Z` = (const CharPosInfo&, const ASString&, const ArrayLH<SwfEvent*>*, const void*, unsigned, unsigned long, CharacterCreateInfo*, InteractiveObject*) -> DisplayObjectBase*, i.e. this + 8.
Disassembly proves the frame and every stack read. Entry homes r8/r9, so the standard slot layout holds: `0x140f01b10 mov qword [rsp+0x20], r9` / `0x140f01b15 mov qword [rsp+0x18], r8`. Six pushes then `0x140f01b24 lea rbp,[rsp-7]` => rbp = entry_rsp-0x37, so [rbp+0x5f]=arg5, [rbp+0x67]=arg6, [rbp+0x6f]=arg7, [rbp+0x77]=arg8, [rbp+0x7f]=arg9. Reads:
  0x140f01b30  mov r12d, dword [rbp+0x6f]   ; arg7 flags, read UNCONDITIONALLY, bit0/bit2 gate the whole function (0x140f01b49 shr ebx,2 ; 0x140f01c2a test bl,bl)
  0x140f01b65  mov rax, qword [rbp+0x77]    ; arg8 CharacterCreateInfo*
  0x140f01b6c  test rax,rax / je 0x140f01b88
  0x140f01b6e  movups xmm0, xmmword [rax]   ; 24-byte deref of arg8 -> AV on garbage-nonzero
  0x140f01b71  movsd  xmm1, qword [rax+0x10]
  0x140f01c05  mov r13d, dword [rbp+0x67]   ; arg6, compared to 0xffffffff
  0x140f01edf  mov rdx,  qword [rbp+0x7f]   ; arg9 InteractiveObject* parent
  0x140f01f36  mov rax,  qword [rbp+0x5f]   ; arg5
.pdata confirms 0x140f01b10 is a real function entry (RUNTIME_FUNCTION 0x140f01b10..0x140f01c22).
recommendation: Redeclare AddDispFn as `void *(void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, uint32_t, uint32_t, void*, void*)` (this, CharPosInfo*, ASString*, ArrayLH<SwfEvent*>*, const void*, unsigned, unsigned long, CharacterCreateInfo*, InteractiveObject*), take all nine in adddisp_detour and forward all nine on both call paths. Nothing in the detour needs args 5-9 - it only reads *(rcx-0x10) and rdx+0x50 - so the fix is purely the signature.
verify_note: Independently reproduced and strengthened. (a) Target identity: the AOB at src/goblin_gfx_probe.cpp:2158 matches EXACTLY ONCE in the image, at 0x140f01b10, and .pdata has RUNTIME_FUNCTION 0x140f01b10..0x140f01c22 (plus a chained continuation 0x140f01c22..0x140f0206d, UNWIND flags 0x4, so 0x140f01edf/0x140f01f36 are the same function). No direct E8/E9 callers -> it is virtual, matching the SDK's `UEAA`. (b) It is AvmSprite::AddDisplayObject, not Sprite::: the LogError string 'Sprite::AddDisplayObject() - unknown cid = %d' at 0x140f01bc1 lives in AvmSprite::AddDisplayObject, C:\Program Files (x86)\Scaleform\GFx SDK 4.0\Src\GFx\AS2\AS2_AvmSprite.cpp:410-440, whose parameter list is (pos, name, peventHandlers, pinitSource, createFrame, addFlags, pcharCreateOverride, origChar) = this + 8. The SDK body maps onto the disassembly line for line: `CharacterCreateInfo ccinfo = pcharCreateOverride ? *pcharCreateOverride : pdefImpl->GetCharacterCreateInfo(pos.CharacterId)` == 0x140f01b65 mov rax,[rbp+0x77] / test / je / movups xmm0,[rax] / movsd xmm1,[rax+0x10] vs. the 0x14116c5f0 call at 0x140f01b97; `createFrame == SF_MAX_UINT` == 0x140f01c05 mov r13d,[rbp+0x67] compared to 0xffffffff; `addFlags & Flags_PlaceObject` / `& Flags_ReplaceIfDepthIsOccupied` == 0x140f01b30 mov r12d,[rbp+0x6f] then and r13b,1 / shr ebx,2 / and bl,1. (c) Frame arithmetic verified: entry homes r9->[rsp+0x20] and r8->[rsp+0x18], 6 pushes then `lea rbp,[rsp-7]` => rbp = entry_rsp-0x37, so [rbp+0x5f/0x67/0x6f/0x77/0x7f] = entry+0x28/0x30/0x38/0x40/0x48 = args 5/6/7/8/9. My scripted stack-slot scan over the function (validated against 11 other targets that produce zero hits) flags exactly the arg6/arg7/arg8 reads. (d) THE DECISIVE NEW EVIDENCE the finding only argued indirectly: I disassembled our own compiled detour. In BUILDS/build/Release/MapForGoblins.dll (and the same AOB string is present in releases/pre-release-err/MapForGoblins.dll, i.e. this ships), adddisp_detour is at 0x1800c00d0 (found via the rip-lea at 0x1800c024e to the '[rehost] ADDDISP place charId=' string, resolved to its RUNTIME_FUNCTION 0x1800c00d0..0x1800c02ed). Prologue: 4 arg homings, 5 pushes, `sub rsp,0xc0` => rsp = entry-0xE8. The live exit is `0x1800c02c8 mov rax,[0x1806f0a50] / mov r9,r14 / mov r8,r15 / mov rdx,rbx / mov rcx,rdi / 0x1800c02db call rax / add rsp,0xc0 / pops / ret` - a REAL CALL, not a tail jmp. So the callee reads its args 5..9 at entry-0xC0..entry-0xA0, deep inside our own frame, never the caller's stack-arg area.
corrected: The defect is real but the finding's mechanism for why MSVC cannot tail-jmp is wrong: g_ms_watch_cid is only ever loaded (src/goblin_gfx_probe.cpp:240 decl, :488 and :1281 loads) and never stored, so the `return r` path at :498 is dead - the compiler simply did not tail-call the single live `return o_adddisp(...)`. Also more specific than 'garbage': the callee's arg8 (pcharCreateOverride) slot is call_rsp+0x40 = entry-0xA8, which is bit-for-bit the same address our detour uses as the movieDef safe-read buffer (0x1800c011b mov [rsp+0x40],rax then the 8-byte read at 0x1800c0130), so during the pre-capture window arg8 is a live movieDef pointer -> the engine takes the *pcharCreateOverride branch with a bogus 24-byte CharacterCreateInfo instead of the dict lookup. Caveat worth recording: this ships in the released err DLL and no mass crash is reported, which static analysis cannot explain; the deciding runtime observation is to log the 5 qwords at rsp+0x28..0x48 immediately before the trampoline call (or break at 0x140f01b65 with the DLL loaded) and see what arg7/arg8/arg9 actually hold.

title: DrawingContext moveTo/lineTo declared (this,int,int) but the engine reads the coordinates from xmm1/xmm2
our_code: src/goblin_stall_probe.cpp:378-379 (DcMoveToFn / DcLineToFn = void(void*, int, int)); resolved at src/goblin_stall_probe.cpp:7590 and 7593
claim: We model the 2nd and 3rd arguments of the two DrawingContext path primitives as integers (twips). Both functions read them as floats out of xmm1/xmm2, so a call built from our typedef would pass the values in edx/r8d and leave xmm1/xmm2 holding whatever the caller left there. This is exactly the defect class of the already-found dialog-update bug, in the opposite direction (int declared where the ABI puts a float).
evidence:
lineTo, resolved to 0x14119d7a0:
  0x14119d7a5  test byte [rcx+0xd0], 8
  0x14119d7b5  movaps xmm6, xmm2        ; arg3 is a float
  0x14119d7bd  movaps xmm7, xmm1        ; arg2 is a float
  0x14119d7e2  movaps xmm3, xmm6 / 0x14119d7e5 movaps xmm2, xmm7 ; passed on as floats
  0x14119d7fb  movss dword [rbx+0xc0], xmm7 ; stored as the float current-x
moveTo, resolved to 0x14119d690:
  0x14119d6bd  movaps xmm6, xmm2
  0x14119d6f5  movaps xmm7, xmm1
  0x14119d758  movaps xmm2, xmm6
Contrast with the sibling helper we DID model correctly, clip_set_scale 0x140733280: `0x14073329f movaps xmm7, xmm2 / 0x1407332a2 movaps xmm6, xmm1` and src/goblin_stall_probe.cpp:2370 declares `void(void*, float, float)`.
beginFill 0x14119cc20 reads no xmm at all (`0x14119cc36 mov ebx, edx` -> `0x14119cc70 mov dword [rdi+0x40], ebx`), so DcBeginFillFn's uint32_t is right; begin 0x14119cb50 `movzx edi, dl` matches its `char`; endFill 0x14119d650 and shapeReset 0x14119d0c0 take rcx only.
recommendation: Change both typedefs to `void(void*, float, float)`. Currently dormant: grep shows g_dc_moveto/g_dc_lineto are resolved and null-checked at 7590-7607 but never called (the solid-fill spike was never written), so nothing misbehaves today - fix the typedefs before anyone writes the first call.
verify_note: The type claim is right and I reproduced every instruction. lineTo AOB (src/goblin_stall_probe.cpp:7593) resolves to 0x14119d7a0: `0x14119d7a6 test byte [rcx+0xd0],8 / 0x14119d7ad mov rbx,rcx / 0x14119d7b5 movaps xmm6,xmm2 / 0x14119d7bd movaps xmm7,xmm1 / 0x14119d7e2 movaps xmm3,xmm6 / 0x14119d7e5 movaps xmm2,xmm7 / 0x14119d7fb movss [rbx+0xc0],xmm7 / 0x14119d808 movss [rbx+0xc4],xmm6`. moveTo AOB (:7590) resolves to 0x14119d690: `0x14119d6bd movaps xmm6,xmm2 / 0x14119d6f5 movaps xmm7,xmm1`. Both take (this, float, float); my stack scan shows no arg beyond the registers, so arity is exactly 3. `void(void*, int, int)` at src/goblin_stall_probe.cpp:378-379 is therefore the wrong type in the right slots.
corrected: Right about the wrong model, wrong about the risk. g_dc_moveto / g_dc_lineto (and g_dc_begin/beginfill/endfill/shapereset) are NEVER invoked anywhere in src/ - grep shows only the typedefs (378-385), the modutils::scan assignments (7585-7599), the all-or-nothing null gate (7602-7605) and the address log (7612-7614). No call is ever built from the typedef, so xmm1/xmm2 are never left stale and there is no wrong-behaviour risk today; the risk is 'none / latent trap for whoever first writes the call'. The claim that this is 'exactly the defect class of the dialog-update bug' overstates it: the dialog bug was a live hook on a hot path.

title: Nine detours declare more parameters than the target reads - harmless as forwarded, but each is a wrong model of the function
our_code: src/goblin_maphover.cpp:60 (BuildFn 4), src/goblin_stall_probe.cpp:5155 (AppendTabFn 4), src/goblin_stall_probe.cpp:78 + 7481-7492 (Fn4 on 10 targets), src/goblin_stall_probe.cpp:6550 (jobpoll Fn4), src/goblin_gfx_probe.cpp:77 (SpriteLoaderFn 2), src/goblin_gfx_probe.cpp:93 (ExecFn 3), src/goblin_map_timing.cpp:39 (Fn 4)
claim: Each of these declares N parameters where the callee reads fewer. Forwarding the extra registers unchanged is safe here (the callee never reads them as inputs, only reuses them as scratch), but the declarations record a signature the engine does not have, which is how bogus diagnostics get built on a phantom argument.
evidence:
Real argument reads, from each target's prologue:
  maphover BuildFn 0x140a82a80: only rcx (`mov r15,rcx`) and rdx (`mov eax,[rdx+0x34]`, `mov r12,[rdx+0x48]`); [rbp+0x40/0x48/0x50] (= arg1/2/3 home slots) are WRITTEN as scratch, never read as inputs -> 2 args, we declare 4.
  AppendTabFn 0x140967b50: `mov rdi,rdx` / `mov rbx,rcx` only; r8/r9 untouched -> 2 args, we declare 4 (and pass nullptr,nullptr at goblin_stall_probe.cpp:5199, which is only safe because of this).
  SpriteLoaderFn 0x1411e2bc0: rdx is overwritten at 0x1411e2c02 (`mov rdx,[rbx+0x60]`) before any read -> 1 arg, we declare 2.
  RM2 ExecFn 0x1411bde10: `0x1411bde10 mov qword [rsp+0x18], rbx` uses arg3's home slot as a register save, reads only rcx/rdx, and `0x1411bde31 mov r8,[rbx+0x30]` reuses r8 -> 2 args, we declare 3 (already documented in docs/research_retired_native_ui_experiments.md).
  map_timing Fn 0x1410d97b0: `mov rbx,rcx` only -> 1 arg, we declare 4.
  jobpoll 0x140e811c0: `sub rsp,0x28 / mov rcx,[rcx]` only -> 1 arg, we declare 4.
  Fn4 counter targets: 0x1411d3980 reads rcx only; 0x14117e140 reads rcx+rdx; 0x140d716a0 reads rcx only; 0x1411577b0 reads rcx/rdx/r8; 0x140d7d720 reads rdx/r8; 0x14115cde0 reads rcx/rdx; 0x14113feb0 reads rcx/rdx/r8b; 0x1410dbb70 reads rcx/rdx/r8; 0x1410dbea0 and 0x1410dc260 read all four.
None of these read any stack argument: range-limited greps over each function's .pdata extent found no access at entry_rsp+0x28 or above.
recommendation: Trim each typedef to the real arity (or leave it and add the real arity in the comment). No behavioural change; do it so the next reader does not infer a 4th argument that does not exist.
verify_note: Every sub-claim reproduced. maphover BuildFn 0x140a82a80: 7 pushes then `mov rbp,rsp` (rbp=entry-0x38); reads only rcx (`mov r15,rcx`) and rdx (`mov eax,[rdx+0x34]`, `mov r12,[rdx+0x48]`); [rbp+0x40/0x48/0x50] = entry+0x08/0x10/0x18 = the arg1/2/3 home slots, written as scratch. AppendTab 0x140967b50: `mov rdi,rdx` / `mov rbx,rcx` only; r8/r9 are reloaded as scratch for the DLFixedVector assert paths (`lea r8,[0x143295988] "out of memory."`), so the live call `o_append_tab(listBase, catBuf, nullptr, nullptr)` at :5199 is genuinely safe. SpriteLoader 0x1411e2bc0: rdx dead-overwritten at 0x1411e2c02 `mov rdx,[rbx+0x60]`. RM2 Execute 0x1411bde10: `mov [rsp+0x18],rbx` uses arg3's home slot as a register save, reads rcx/rdx only, `0x1411bde31 mov r8,[rbx+0x30]` reuses r8. map_timing 0x1410d97b0: `mov rbx,rcx` only, arg1/arg2 home slots used to save rbx/rsi. jobpoll 0x140e811c0: `sub rsp,0x28 / mov rcx,[rcx]` only. All 10 Fn4 AOBs (src/goblin_stall_probe.cpp:7470-7481) resolve uniquely to exactly the addresses listed. The load-bearing 'no stack args' claim I re-derived mechanically rather than by grep: a scripted rsp/rbp tracker over each function's full chained-.pdata chunk set (typed-find 3 chunks, child-step 3, xform-get 3, item-proc 5, next-capture 6, rm2exec 3, plus the single-chunk ones) found ZERO accesses at entry_rsp+0x28 or above. The same scanner correctly flags the arg6/arg7/arg8 reads in AddDisplayObject and the arg5 read in DisplayList::AddDisplayObject(5), so it is not blind.
corrected: Two immaterial errors in the evidence. (1) maphover: [rbp+0x40/0x48/0x50] are the arg1/arg2/arg3 home slots (entry+0x08/0x10/0x18), not arg1/2/3 in the sense of the stack-arg area - the point stands. (2) batch-job 0x140d7d720 is described as 'reads rdx/r8', but its prologue is `mov rdi,r8 / mov rsi,rdx / call ...` with rcx left untouched and consumed by the inner call, so rcx is an input too. Neither changes the conclusion: all nine are over-declarations, forwarding is safe, risk none.

title: goblin_maphover_probe installs a second MinHook on the same target as goblin_maphover, but setup() is never called
our_code: src/goblin_maphover_probe.cpp:106 (hook on the same AOB as src/goblin_maphover.cpp:667); no caller - dllmain.cpp:115-119 registers map_timing/gfx_probe/maphover/stall_probe/worldmap_probe only
claim: Both files hook the same function. Today this is inert because maphover_probe::setup() has no caller, so the duplicate never happens. If it is ever wired up, the second MH_CreateHook on the same target returns MH_ERROR_ALREADY_CREATED, modutils::hook throws (src/modutils.cpp:101), and only the log line changes - but whichever setup runs second silently gets no probe.
evidence: Both AOBs resolve to the same unique address: src/goblin_maphover.cpp:667 and src/goblin_maphover_probe.cpp:107 both match exactly once, at 0x14087a8e0 (verified by byte-pattern scan over the whole image; 1 hit each). Disassembly at 0x14087a8e0 confirms 3 args: `0x14087a916 mov rdi,r8 / 0x14087a919 mov rbx,rdx / 0x14087a91c mov r13,rcx`, matching PlaceNameFn = void*(void*,void*,void*) in both files.
recommendation: Either delete goblin_maphover_probe.cpp or make its setup() reuse goblin::maphover's trampoline instead of installing a second hook on the same address.
verify_note: All factual assertions verified. The AOBs at src/goblin_maphover.cpp:667 and src/goblin_maphover_probe.cpp:107 are byte-identical and match exactly once in the image, at 0x14087a8e0, whose prologue is `0x14087a916 mov rdi,r8 / 0x14087a919 mov rbx,rdx / 0x14087a91c mov r13,rcx` with no stack-arg access anywhere in 0x14087a8e0..0x14087abea - 3 args, matching PlaceNameFn in both files. maphover_probe::setup() has no caller (grep over src/ finds only its own definition at :101 and the header decl in goblin_maphover_probe.hpp:6; dllmain.cpp:105-119 registers map_timing/gfx_probe/maphover/stall_probe/worldmap_probe). modutils::hook does throw on any non-MH_OK from MH_CreateHook (src/modutils.cpp:99-103), so the described failure mode is accurate.
corrected: Stronger than stated: it is not merely uncalled, it is not compiled. CMakeLists.txt uses an explicit source list (add_library at line 95) and lists only src/goblin_maphover.hpp / .cpp at lines 157-158; src/goblin_maphover_probe.cpp appears nowhere, so the translation unit is absent from every built DLL. Wiring it up would require a CMake change as well as a setup() call, making this dead source rather than a latent runtime hazard.

claim: This is the already-found defect #1 site. Verified fixed: the second slot really is a float in xmm1 and the third really is a byte pointer in r8.

verify_note: OK-VERIFIED stands; re-derived. base+0x93F540 = 0x14093f540 (install src/goblin_stall_probe.cpp:7778). title: OK-VERIFIED: CSMenuMan::updateTask's 2nd argument is a POINTER to a struct with a float at +8, not a float - do not "fix" it to float
our_code: src/goblin_stall_probe.cpp:1660 (MenuUpdateFn = void(void *menuman, void *dt)), :5067 menu_update_detour, installed at :7648
claim: The parameter name `dt` invites someone to change this to `float dt` by analogy with form_update. That would be wrong: rdx is a real pointer and xmm1 is not read at entry.
evidence: 0x140766980: `0x1407669bb mov rdi, rdx` / `0x1407669be mov rbx, rcx`; the float is loaded THROUGH rdx: `0x1407669e7 subss xmm0, dword [rdx+8]` and `0x140766a1a movss xmm1, dword [rdi+8]`. xmm1 is only ever written, never read on entry. No access at entry_rsp+0x28 or above anywhere in 0x140766980..0x140767177, so the arity is 2. Returns void (`0x140767176 ret` with no rax set).
recommendation: No change. Consider renaming the parameter to `dtCtx` so nobody "fixes" it.
verify_note: OK-VERIFIED stands. 0x140766980 prologue `mov rax,rsp / 8 pushes / lea rbp,[rax-0x5f] / sub rsp,0x98`, then `0x1407669bb mov rdi,rdx / 0x1407669be mov rbx,rcx`. xmm1 is never read on entry: xmm6-xmm10 are spilled, `0x1407669c1 xorps xmm7,xmm7`, and the only xmm1 touch is a WRITE from the pointer, `0x140766a1a movss xmm1,dword [rdi+8]`. The delta-time is loaded THROUGH rdx: `0x1407669e7 subss xmm0,dword [rdx+8]`. Arity 2: my scan over the whole single chunk 0x140766980..0x140767177 finds no access at entry+0x28 or above. Void return: the epilogue is `0x140767163 add rsp,0x98 / pop r15,r14,r13,r12,rdi,rsi,rbx,rbp / 0x140767176 ret` with no rax set. Changing the 2nd parameter to float would indeed be a regression.

title: OK-VERIFIED: the world->map converter's 3rd argument really is uint32_t* (an in/out pointer), not the packed id by value
our_code: src/goblin_worldmap_probe.cpp:21 (ConvertFn = char(void*, Vec2*, uint32_t*, Vec3*)), :36 seh_fold passes &p
claim: The comment at goblin_worldmap_probe.cpp:18 describes r8 as "packed id {area<<24|...}", which reads as a by-value argument while the typedef is a pointer. The pointer is correct, and passing a local copy is also correct because the callee can rewrite it.
evidence: 0x1408877d0 forwards r8 unchanged (`0x1408877f1 mov r12,r8` -> `0x14088782a mov r8,r12`) into 0x140876140, which dereferences it: `0x14087616d mov eax, dword [r8]` and then re-reads a possibly-updated copy at `0x140876196 mov eax, dword [rsp+0x30]` after calling 0x1408775e0 with `0x140876189 mov r9,r8`. r9 is likewise a pointer (`0x140876156 mov eax,[r9+8]`, `0x140876164 movsd xmm0, qword [r9]`), matching Vec3*. 4 args, no stack args.
recommendation: No change; reword the comment to say "r8 = pointer to the packed id (callee may rewrite it)".
verify_note: OK-VERIFIED stands. 0x1408877d0 reads all four registers and forwards r8/r9 unchanged (`0x1408877ee mov r15,r9 / 0x1408877f1 mov r12,r8 / 0x1408877f4 mov r13,rdx / 0x1408877f7 mov rsi,rcx` then `0x14088782a mov r8,r12 / 0x14088782d mov rdx,r13 / 0x140887824 mov r9,r15 / 0x140887830 call 0x140876140`); my scan over 0x1408877d0..0x14088786c finds no stack args, so arity 4. The callee dereferences both: `0x14087616d mov eax,dword [r8]` (u32 through the pointer) and `0x140876156 mov eax,[r9+8]` / `0x140876164 movsd xmm0,qword [r9]` (Vec3 through the pointer). title: GEOF 8-byte record: bit 0 IS the stored boolean, and we ignore it - a "not collected" record is decoded as collected
our_code: src/goblin_collected.cpp:266-276 (entry decode: entry[1] flags, entry[2..3] geom_idx, entry[4..7] model_hash; entry[0] never inspected)
claim: We assume: every 8-byte record present in a tile's GeomFlagSaveData blob means "this geom is collected/destroyed" (the only filter is entry_flags in {0x00,0x80}). Actually: the record is `key | value` where key = ((model_id<<0x11)|geom_idx)<<0xf (bits 15..63) and bit 0 is the stored BOOLEAN. The engine's setter leaves a record in place and CLEARS bit 0 when the value goes false, and the tile-load applier only marks an instance collected when bit 0 is set. title: Grown SpriteDef::Playlist buffer comes from the CRT heap but Scaleform frees it through its own MemoryHeap

  0x1411be2b6  mov rax,[rcx] ; 0x1411be2b9 call qword [rax+0x60]   ; <-- FREE of Playlist.Data

title: Manual refcount arithmetic at DisplayObject+8 is the correct offset and correctly non-atomic
claim: This looks like an unsynchronised read-modify-write on an engine refcount, i.e. a race. The SDK says otherwise: the class's own AddRef is a plain non-atomic `RefCount++`, so a raw `++` is exactly equivalent to calling it, and there is no atomic contract to violate. The offset is also right: RefCount is the first member after the vptr.

SDK: `DisplayObjectBase : public RefCountBaseWeakSupport<...>` (Src/GFx/GFx_DisplayObject.h:113) -> `RefCountBaseStatImpl<RefCountWeakSupportImpl, Stat>` (Src/Kernel/SF_RefCount.h:234) -> `RefCountWeakSupportImpl : RefCountNTSImpl : RefCountImplCore`. `RefCountImplCore` holds `volatile int RefCount` as its only data member behind a virtual dtor (SF_RefCount.h:70-76) => offset +8 on x64. `RefCountNTSImpl::AddRef() { RefCount++; }` (SF_RefCount.h:122) - explicitly the non-thread-safe variant, unlike `RefCountImpl` whose AddRef is atomic. Note also that AddRef/Release are NOT virtual, so there is no vtable slot to call instead.
Thread ownership is separately self-checked: v3_check_owner (src/goblin_stall_probe.cpp:1226-1240) latches the first mutator thread and logs an error if a second one appears, and the only callers reach it via v3_native_tick (src/goblin_stall_probe.cpp:1420-1426, driven from the map frame at :7292).

verify_note: Accurate. SDK chain verified: DisplayObjectBase : RefCountBaseWeakSupport<> (Src/GFx/GFx_DisplayObject.h:113) -> RefCountBaseStatImpl<RefCountWeakSupportImpl,...> (Src/Kernel/SF_RefCount.h:234) -> RefCountWeakSupportImpl : RefCountNTSImpl : RefCountImplCore, whose only data member is `volatile int RefCount` behind a virtual dtor (SF_RefCount.h:69-76) => +8 on x64, and `RefCountNTSImpl::AddRef() { RefCount++; }` (SF_RefCount.h:122) is explicitly the non-atomic variant (the atomic one is RefCountImpl, SF_RefCount.h:110-114). title: Rebuilt FMG bank installed in a MsgRepository slot comes from GetProcessHeap(), and the free path is unknown
claim: We overwrite an engine-owned MsgRepository slot pointer with a buffer of our own. The buffer the slot held was produced by the game's msgbnd/BND loader, not by the CRT. If anything in the engine ever releases that slot (language switch, msgbnd reload, repository teardown) it will do so with whichever allocator loaded it, and our CRT/process-heap pointer becomes a cross-allocator free - the same failure mode as the SpriteDef Playlist finding, which is confirmed elsewhere in this dimension.
evidence: Our allocation is unambiguously the process heap (goblin_messages.cpp:327). The slot is engine memory: `sub = base_array[0]` derives from the live MsgRepositoryImp singleton at 0x143d7d4f8, whose slot indexing is proven by 0x14266d3c0 (`mov rax,[rcx+8]; mov rcx,[rax+rdx*8]; mov rcx,[rcx+r8*8]`). I did not locate any code that frees a slot entry, so I cannot show the free happens - only that if it does, the allocator will not be ours. Note also that `static void *fmg_allocation` (goblin_messages.cpp:35) is a single global reused by every patch call, so we do not even retain the pointers we install.
recommendation: Keep the original slot pointer (already done for PlaceName via g_vanilla_placename_fmg at :1284) for every patched slot, and restore all of them from a DLL detach / repository-teardown hook so the engine only ever frees a pointer it allocated. Separately, confirm the teardown by breaking on the MsgRepositoryImp dtor once; if it does free slot entries, the correct fix is to patch the existing buffer in place (extend nothing) rather than swap the pointer.
verify_note: Both halves of the risk remain unproven, and one relevant fact cuts against the claim while another cuts for it. Against: our buffer is HeapAlloc(GetProcessHeap()) and the game's statically linked UCRT malloc/free use RtlAllocateHeap/HeapFree on the handle at 0x144858510 (0x14254a43c, and the realloc at 0x14254a4fa) - in the UCRT that handle is the process heap, so a free by the game's own CRT free would be allocator-compatible, not corrupting. For: the MsgRepository does not use the CRT - its arrays come from an allocator OBJECT at repo+0x30 through a vtable slot (0x14266d52e-0x14266d54b `mov rcx,[rbx+0x30]; mov rax,[rcx]; call qword [rax+0x50]`), so if the FMG file buffers come from the same DLKR-style allocator, a release of a slot entry would go through its Free slot and our process-heap pointer would be foreign to it. I could not find any code that frees an individual sub-array slot entry (the region's `call [rax+0x68]` sites disassemble as misaligned linear noise without analysis, so I cannot rule one out either). What would decide it statically: locate the msgbnd (re)load/teardown path - e.g. the language-switch handler that repopulates repo sub-arrays - and see whether it releases the previous slot pointer. Runtime test: apply the patch, change the game language (or force a msgbnd reload) and watch for a fault/heap check inside that allocator's Free. Also worth fixing independently of the verdict: `static void *fmg_allocation` (goblin_messages.cpp:35) is one global reused by every patch call, so earlier buffers are unreachable and unrestorable.

title: draw_raw AddRefs resource+8 on a stub that already does `add rcx,8` - the refcount is never bumped and a pointer field is incremented instead
claim: We assume `kAddRef = 0x113BB70` takes the ADDRESS OF THE COUNTER, so we pass `resource + 8`. It actually takes the OBJECT pointer and adds 8 itself.
evidence:
AddRef stub, function start confirmed (preceded by a terminating jmp at 0x14113bb6b):
  0x14113bb70  add rcx, 8
  0x14113bb74  mov edx, 1
  0x14113bb79  jmp 0x141140bb0
  0x141140bb0  lock xadd dword [rcx], edx     ; interlocked +1 at (arg+8)
Matching Release stub takes the object too:
  0x14113bb90  mov rbx, rcx ; add rcx, 8 ; or edx,-1 ; call 0x141140bb0
  ... 0x14113bbaa  mov rcx, qword [rbx + 0x10]  ; +0x10 is a POINTER field, dereferenced on the destruct path
ImageResource base ctor puts the counter at +8 and the pointer at +0x10:
  0x140d5fe10  mov dword [rcx + 8], 1
  0x140d5fe19  mov qword [rcx + 0x10], rdx   ; rdx = 0
The engine's own drawImageInto caller passes the OBJECT, not object+8:

  0x14074bf4f  call 0x14113bb70
and drawImageInto Releases *res on BOTH exits (0x140d818bd success, 0x140d818ce failure) with `mov rcx,[rsi]` (object, no +8).

As written the call does `lock xadd dword [resource+0x10], 1`, corrupting the low dword of the resource's owner pointer (it starts as 0, so it becomes 1), while the real refcount at resource+8 stays at 1; drawImageInto's unconditional Release then takes it 1 -> 0, runs the destruct path, loads `rcx = [resource+0x10] == 1` and dereferences address 1.   0x14113bb70  add rcx, 8
  0x14113bb74  mov edx, 1
  0x14113bb79  jmp 0x141140bb0
  0x141140bb0  lock xadd dword [rcx], edx ; 0x141140bb4 mov eax,edx ; ret

The matching Release 0x14113bb90 does `mov rbx,rcx; add rcx,8; or edx,-1; call 0x141140bb0` and drawImageInto calls it as `mov rcx, qword [rsi]` (0x140d818b5 success / 0x140d818c6 failure) with rsi = rdx = arg2 = &res -> the object, no +8.

title: Appended frame array is CRT-malloc'd but the engine frees it with Scaleform::MemoryHeap::Free
our_code: src/goblin_gfx_probe.cpp:208 (gfx_alloc), :1245-1256 (frame-array grow), :180-186 (the comment asserting the wrong contract)
claim: We assume: "The frame array ... are OWNED by Scaleform: it FREES them (CRT free -> _free_base) ... So these buffers MUST come from the GAME's own _malloc_base" (comment at :180-186), so gfx_alloc uses the game's CRT malloc for the replacement frame-playlist buffer written to spriteDef+0x38. Truth: that buffer is allocated, reallocated and freed EXCLUSIVELY through the Scaleform global MemoryHeap at exe+0x4593250 - never through the CRT. A CRT-malloc'd pointer handed to MemoryHeap::Free is a foreign pointer; the heap resolves its page/segment bookkeeping from the pointer itself.
evidence: SpriteDef destructor 0x1411be250: after destroying each frame's tags it frees the array -> 0x1411be2ab `mov rcx, qword [0x144593250]`; 0x1411be2b2 `mov rdx, qword [rdi + 0x38]`; 0x1411be2b9 `call qword [rax + 0x60]`. The array's own capacity helper 0x1411bfb00 uses the SAME object for all three operations: 0x1411bfb2a `mov rcx,[0x144593250]` / 0x1411bfb34 `call [rax+0x60]` (Free when newCap==0), 0x1411bfb67 `call [rax+0x58]` (Realloc, rdx=oldData r8=newBytes), 0x1411bfb8f `call [rax+0x70]` with r9=&AllocInfo{0x108} (AllocAutoHeap for the first alloc). Slot->method mapping proven from the SDK declaration order in C:\Program Files (x86)\Scaleform\GFx SDK 4.0\Src\Kernel\SF_MemoryHeap.h (class MemoryHeap, line 86ff): dtor=+0x00, CreateArena +0x08, DestroyArena +0x10, ArenaIsEmpty +0x18, CreateHeap +0x20, SetLimitHandler +0x28, SetLimit +0x30, AddRef +0x38, Release +0x40, Alloc(size,info) +0x48, Alloc(size,align,info) +0x50, Realloc +0x58, Free(ptr) +0x60, AllocAutoHeap(this,size,info) +0x68, AllocAutoHeap(this,size,align,info) +0x70 - and the call sites' argument shapes match exactly. Array layout also confirmed: 0x1411bfbb0 Resize reads size at [rcx+8] and capacity at [rcx+0x10] on an array object located at spriteDef+0x38 (0x1411be382 `lea r14, [r15+0x38]`), i.e. Data@+0x38 / Size@+0x40 / Capacity@+0x48. Reachability: vanilla sprite 171 has 348 frames and capacity 348 (Resize rounds capacity to a multiple of 4: 0x1411bfb50 `lea rdi,[r8+3]` / `and rdi,~3`), so the very first icon append takes the `target > fcap` grow branch on every worldmap load, for every profile (frame counts 348/376/441/906 in the five shipped 02_120_worldmap.gfx). The project already resolves the right allocator elsewhere: src/goblin_sfimage.cpp:89 `constexpr uintptr_t kHeapPtr = 0x4593250; // Scaleform MemoryHeap*, vt+0x50 = Alloc`.
recommendation: Allocate the replacement frame array from the same heap the engine will free it with: heap = *(void**)(base+0x4593250), then either vt[+0x48] Alloc(size, nullptr) or, to match the engine byte for byte, vt[+0x70] AllocAutoHeap(sd, bytes, 0, &AllocInfo{0x108}). Keep gfx_alloc (CRT) only for the tag objects and per-frame tag-pointer arrays, which the engine never frees (see the OK-VERIFIED note on Frame::DestroyTags), and correct the comment at :180-186. Also note the original engine-allocated array leaks once we overwrite spriteDef+0x38.
verify_note: Re-ran every step. SpriteDef dtor 0x1411be250: 0x1411be269 `cmp qword [rcx+0x40], rbx` / loop 0x1411be280 `shl rax,4; add rax,[rdi+0x38]; call 0x1412449b0` (per-frame element, stride 0x10), then 0x1411be2ab `mov rcx,[0x144593250]` / 0x1411be2b2 `mov rdx,[rdi+0x38]` / 0x1411be2b9 `call [rax+0x60]`. Capacity helper 0x1411bfb00 uses the same global for all three ops: +0x60 Free (rdx=data, newCap==0), +0x58 with rcx=heap rdx=oldData r8=newBytes = Realloc(oldPtr,newSize), +0x70 with rdx=thisPtr r8=size r9=&{0x108} = AllocAutoHeap. Realloc(+0x58) and Free(+0x60) are the only non-overloaded slots in that region of SF_MemoryHeap.h (virtuals at :300,331,332,333,342,371,372,387,394,406,407,411,412,416,420) and their argument shapes match exactly, so the mapping does not depend on MSVC's overload ordering. HeapPT_MemoryHeap.cpp:645-658 shows Free resolving the owning segment from the pointer itself (`HeapPT::GlobalPageTable->GetSegment(UPInt(ptr))`, assert compiled out in release, then `seg->pHeap`) - a CRT-malloc'd pointer is not in that page table. Our replacement buffer at spriteDef+0x38 comes from gfx_alloc (src/goblin_gfx_probe.cpp:208, the AOB at :176 is MSVC `malloc`: `cmp rcx,-0x20 / ja / test rcx,rcx / mov eax,1 / cmove` then _malloc_base + _callnewh retry) and is installed at :1255 `wr64(sd+OFF_FRAMEARR_DATA, arr)`. The per-frame tag-pointer array and the synthesized tags are never freed - the frame-element dtor 0x1412449b0 iterates [rbx+0]/[rbx+8], calls each tag's slot-0 deleting dtor with `xor edx,edx` (0x1412449d3) so the flag&1 delete branch at 0x140ee3e13 / 0x140ee3da4 is skipped, then just nulls Data/Size at 0x1412449e7 without freeing. So the comment's 'the frame array, per-frame tag-pointer arrays, and synthesized tags ... it FREES them' is wrong twice: only the frame array is freed, and it is freed through Scaleform's MemoryHeap, never the CRT.

title: vtable+0x30 is AddToTimelineSnapshot, not ExecuteTag::Execute - every label, constant and diagnostic in the tag path names the wrong function
our_code: src/goblin_gfx_probe.cpp:336-349 (the vtable/Execute constant block), :1114 (rm2exec_detour), :1513 / :1799 / :1846 / :1880 (rq(vt + 0x30) called as "Execute"), :2196-2199 (hook install on RVA 0x11BDE10)

And 0x1411bf110 is MakeSnapshot: per frame `call [rax+0x58]` on rdx (GetPlaylist -> out at [rsp+0x20], count [rsp+0x28]) then per tag `rcx=tag; rdx=rsi(snapshot); r8d=edi(frame); call [rax+0x30]` = GFx_SpriteDef.cpp:244-257 verbatim. title: PO3 flags1 bit 0x10 (HasImage) is never read by this build, so build_clean_place_tag and build_clean_sprite_place_tag are identical
claim: We assume flags1=0x10 makes the engine "instantiate charId as a bitmap-image leaf" and flags1=0x00 makes it "a MovieClip that exposes the DrawingContext getter (vtbl+0x2a0)". Truth: PlaceObject3's HasImage bit is parsed by nobody - the resulting character type is decided entirely by what is registered under charId.
evidence: PlaceObject3Tag::Unpack for this build = 0x1411bd3b0 (PO3 vtable 0x142C65D20 slot 8). Full sweep of its flag tests: `test r15b, 8` @0x1411bd441 (HasClassName), `test bl,r15b` (bl=1) @0x1411bd5a4 (HasFilters), `test r15b, 2` @0x1411bd622 (HasBlendMode), `test r15b, 4` @0x1411bd65b (BitmapCaching), `test r15b, 0x20` @0x1411bd71a. r15 is po3Flags (loaded at 0x1411bd414 `movzx r15d, byte [r13+r8]`). Bit 0x10 is never tested anywhere in the function. Same in the SDK: PlaceObject3Tag::Unpack / GetFlags (Src/GFx/GFx_SpriteDef.cpp:1138 and :1057) read PO3_HasClassName/HasFilters/HasBlendMode/BitmapCaching only, and PO3_HasImage (GFx_MovieDef.h:1904) has no reader anywhere in Src/.
recommendation: Collapse the two builders into one (keep flags1=0x10 for byte-parity with the authored native tags, since capture_tag_vtables uses that byte as its PO3 discriminator) and drop the "HasImage -> bitmap leaf" rationale from the comments so nobody debugs a difference that cannot exist.
verify_note: Independently confirmed 0x1411bd3b0 is PlaceObject3Tag::Unpack: it is PO3 vtable slot +0x40, and PO3::Execute (0x1411bd910, slot +0x08) reaches it via `call [rax+0x40]` after building the UnpackedData, matching GFx_SpriteDef.cpp:1002 `Unpack(data)`; GFxPlaceObjectBase adds Unpack/UnpackEventHandlers/GetFlags as the first three new virtuals (GFx_MovieDef.h:1710-1714), i.e. +0x40/+0x48/+0x50. In the body r13=this+8=pData, sil=pData[0]=po2Flags, r8=1 or 9 (`cmovs` on the sign of po2Flags = the HasActions long form), r15d=pData[r8]=po3Flags (0x1411bd414). I dumped all 252 instructions to the ret at 0x1411bd7c1 and swept every test/and: on r15b only `test r15b,8` (0x1411bd441), `test bl,r15b` with bl=1 (0x1411bd5a4), `test r15b,2` (0x1411bd622), `test r15b,4` (0x1411bd65b), `test r15b,0x20` (0x1411bd71a). Bit 0x10 is never tested. GetFlags 0x1411bd8a0 likewise masks po2Flags with 0x5f and tests only po3Flags bits 1, 2 and 0x20. SDK side: `grep -rn PO3_HasImage Src/` returns exactly one hit, the enumerator itself at GFx_MovieDef.h:1904 - no reader anywhere, including ComputeDataSize. So build_clean_place_tag (:1385-1401) and build_clean_sprite_place_tag (:1404-1424) differ only in a byte nothing reads, and the rationale at :1828-1832 / goblin_gfx_probe.hpp:92-94 is fiction.
corrected: Add one piece of direct evidence the finding missed, which makes it airtight: the vanilla gfx itself already sets the bit. My parse of sprite 246 in the shipped 02_120_worldmap.gfx gives its single inner PlaceObject3 body as `06 10 01 00 0a 00 c5 00 00 80 00 00`, i.e. flags1=0x10 on a placement of an ordinary DefineShape (char 10). A bit that the exporter sets on a shape placement cannot be a bitmap/MovieClip type selector.

title: create_native_sprite_child returns a SnapshotElement but is documented (and would be used) as a display child with a vtable
claim: We document the return as "the materialized display-list node" that "exposes the DrawingContext getter (vtbl+0x2a0) the solid-fill spike draws into". Truth: the value is the SnapshotElement found by matching `rd32(node+0x14) == depth` in the TimelineSnapshot's sorted array; its +0x00 is `pPrev` (NULL for the first element), not a vtable. Any `rq(node)`-based virtual call on it is an arbitrary-pointer call.
evidence: The Execute-substitute is `rq(vt + 0x30)` = AddToTimelineSnapshot (see finding slot-0x30-is-not-execute), which only inserts/updates a SnapshotElement - 0x1411bdc85 `call 0x1411beed0` (TimelineSnapshot::Add) then 11 tag-pointer stores; it creates no display object. SnapshotElement has no vtable: SDK Src/GFx/GFx_SpriteDef.h:237 `struct SnapshotElement { SnapshotElement* pPrev; SnapshotElement* pNext; unsigned CreateFrame; int Depth; ... }`, and the engine's own field offsets confirm it (Depth@+0x14 per `cmp r9d, dword [rax+0x14]` @0x1411bdbde).

Either delete it or rewrite the contract: to obtain a real display child you must run the materialization driver (the mod's g_v3_mat_driver = ExecuteSnapshot) and capture the child, which is exactly what create_native_icon_instance's caller in goblin_stall_probe.cpp already does.
verify_note: The object identity follows from the verified slot map: create_native_sprite_child (:1833-1869) calls rq(vt+0x30) = PlaceObject3Tag::AddToTimelineSnapshot, then matches `rd32(node+0x14)==depth` in the rq(ctx+0x28) array. That array is TimelineSnapshot::SnapshotSortedArray (0x1411bdbc7 `mov r10,[rbp+0x28]`, count [rbp+0x30], compare `cmp r9d, dword [rax+0x14]` at 0x1411bdbde) and its elements are SnapshotElement, whose first two qwords are pPrev/pNext (GFx_SpriteDef.h:237-243; 0x1411bdebc-0x1411bded8 unlinks via [rdi+0]/[rdi+8] and writes -1 into both). So goblin_gfx_probe.hpp:92-95 and the comment at :1828-1832 describe the return value wrongly, and the header contradicts itself - the sibling declaration at :85-88 for create_native_icon_instance already says 'the timeline record, not a DisplayObject'.

title: swf_matrix silently encodes any scale >= 1.0 as a negative (mirrored) scale - the 16.16 value is masked into 17 signed bits
claim: We assume `round(sx * 65536) & ((1 << 17) - 1)` is a safe encoding of the scale into FB[17]. Truth: SWF MATRIX scale fields are SIGNED fixed 16.16, so 17 bits hold only -1.0 .. +0.99998. scale 1.0 encodes 0x10000, whose bit 16 is the sign bit, and the engine reads it back as -1.0 (a mirrored icon). The mask hides it instead of failing. Same class of bug on translation: nT=12 gives ±2048 twips (±102.4 px) and `tx & 0xFFF` wraps silently past that.
evidence: SDK Src/GFx/GFx_Stream.cpp:971 StreamContext::ReadMatrix -> `unsigned ScaleNbits = ReadUInt(5); pm->Sx() = ReadSInt(ScaleNbits) / 65536.0f;` - ReadSInt, not ReadUInt. Current values are safe (0.50 -> 32768, 0.38 -> 24904; verified by decoding the emitted LOGO_MATRIX {196,194,144,97,72,51,195,124,52}: HasScale=1, NScaleBits=17, ScaleX=24904, HasRotate=0, NTranslateBits=12, tx=ty=-243), and icon_matrix's largest translation is -round(96*0.5*10) = -480. But generate_logo.py:31-33 explicitly invites the failure: "GLOBAL on-map icon scale ... Bump to enlarge ALL custom icons at once". A sibling generator has the same shape with a wider field: tools/generate_menu_icon_tags.py:52-88 matrix_bytes hardcodes NScaleBits=20 (flips at scale >= 8.0, reachable if an alpha-crop leaves max(size) <= 4 for ICON_PX=32).
recommendation: In swf_matrix, size the fields from the values instead of masking: nS = max(2, value.bit_length()+1) for the larger of |round(sx*65536)|,|round(sy*65536)|, nT likewise, and raise on nS/nT > 31. Same in generate_menu_icon_tags.matrix_bytes. At minimum assert -1.0 < scale < 1.0 and |twips| < 2**(nT-1) so a bumped ICON_SCALE_CUSTOM fails the build instead of mirroring every icon.
verify_note: Both halves re-derived. Encoder: I re-implemented tools/generate_logo.py:77-85 and swf_matrix(0.38,0.38,-243,-243) reproduces the committed src/generated_shared/goblin_logo.cpp:6 LOGO_MATRIX = {196,194,144,97,72,51,195,124,52} exactly, so my model of the function is right; round(1.0*65536)&0x1FFFF = 65536 = 0x10000, whose bit 16 is the sign bit of a 17-bit field. Decoder: the game's own ReadMatrix is 0x1411bbd50 (called from PO3 Unpack at 0x1411bd4b3 under `test sil,4` = PO2_HasMatrix, with rdx = &pos+0x20). It reads nbits via 0x1411bbb40 with edx=5, keeps it in ebp, builds the sign mask `lea ecx,[rbp-1]; mov r12d,1; shl r12d,cl` (0x1411bde08-0x1411bfb0e region: 0x1411bbe08-0x1411bbe0e), then `test eax,r12d; je +8; mov ecx,ebp; mov edx,esi(-1); shl edx,cl; or eax,edx` - textbook sign extension - and finally `cvtdq2ps; mulss xmm6` with xmm6 = [0x1429ce8b0] = 0x37800000 = 2^-16. That is ReadSInt(n)/65536.0f, matching GFx_Stream.cpp:971-977. So 0x10000 in 17 bits decodes to exactly -1.0, a mirrored icon. Also verified the sibling: tools/generate_menu_icon_tags.py:63-66 hardcodes NScaleBits=20, so it flips at scale>=8.0 (524288 -> -8.0), and its scale is ICON_PX/max(size) = 32/max(size) (:376, :402) which reaches 8.0 when an alpha-crop leaves max(size)<=4.
corrected: Correct as an encoder defect, but it is latent with zero present impact, so 'wrong-behaviour' overstates it. Nothing shipped is mis-encoded: 0.38 -> 24904 and 0.50 -> 32768 both clear bit 16, and icon_matrix's largest translation is -round(96*0.5*10) = -480 against a 12-bit signed range of +-2048. generate_menu_icon_tags is likewise safe at its only literal scale (1.0 -> 65536, well below the 20-bit sign bit 0x80000). The defect is that nS/nT are fixed constants and the value is masked rather than range-checked or auto-sized, next to a knob (:31-33 'Bump to enlarge ALL custom icons at once') whose first out-of-range value fails silently; note the same file's sibling gets translate right by auto-sizing (`nbits = max(tx.bit_length(), ty.bit_length()) + 1`), which is the fix shape scale needs.

An exporter that never reuses an id across the two families is using one namespace, so kDefineTags (src/goblin_own_movie.cpp:215) omitting 1001/1005/1008/1009 leaves cid_range_free able to answer 'free' for a range a movie actually defines. title: inject_logo_into_plaque copies 0x80 bytes out of a 20-byte tag object
claim: We assume cloning 0x80 bytes of sprite 246's char-10 placement is safe because "a longer matrix just uses spare bytes of the 0x80 clone". The destination reasoning is right; the SOURCE is not - the tag object is 8 (vtable) + 12 (body) = 20 bytes, so the copy reads 108 bytes past it.
evidence: Sprite 246 in both the vanilla and the ERR 02_120_worldmap.gfx contains exactly one placement: tag code 70 (PlaceObject3), body length 12, bytes `06 10 01 00 0a 00 c5 00 00 80 ...` = flags0=0x06, flags1=0x10, depth=1, charId=10, then a 6-byte matrix. So the live PlaceObject3Tag is 8 + 12 = 20 bytes (the tag body is stored verbatim - PO3 tag objects are `UByte pData[1]` right after the vptr, SDK GFx_MovieDef.h:1910, and this build's Unpack indexes pData from this+8 via `lea r13,[rcx+8]` @0x1411bd3cf). The write side is fine: LOGO_MATRIX is 9 bytes at +0xe (body length 15, well inside 0x80), and nothing after the matrix is parsed for flags0=0x06/flags1=0x10.
recommendation: Copy only 0x14 bytes (or better, build the tag from scratch with build_clean_place_tag(logoCharId, 1, LOGO_MATRIX, LOGO_MATRIX_LEN) - the source envelope adds nothing now that flags0/flags1/depth are known constants). safe_copy's __except currently degrades a fault to "no logo", so this is a low-probability AV rather than a certain one, but the over-read is real and pointless.
verify_note: The source size is established from data, not inference. My own parse of the shipped 02_120_worldmap.gfx gives DefineSprite 246 with frameCount=1 and a 22-byte body whose inner tags are exactly: tag 70 len 12 body `06 10 01 00 0a 00 c5 00 00 80 00 00`, then ShowFrame(1) len 0, End(0) len 0. So one PlaceObject3 with a 12-byte body = flags0 0x06, flags1 0x10, depth 1, charId 10, 6-byte matrix. PO3 tag objects store the body inline after the vptr (this build's Unpack does `lea r13,[rcx+8]` at 0x1411bd3cf and indexes pData from there; SDK GFx_MovieDef.h:1911 `UByte pData[1]`), and the loader allocates sizeof(PlaceObject3Tag)+dataSz-1 (GFx_TagLoaders.cpp:966-987 -> GFx_LoadProcess.h:286-289), i.e. ~27 bytes here. src/goblin_gfx_probe.cpp:1633 copies 0x80 = 128 bytes from it, so ~101 bytes are read past the object. Confirmed.
corrected: Real over-read, but the claimed crash risk does not survive: this cannot fault in practice and cannot corrupt anything. (a) Tag memory comes from DataAllocator, a bump allocator handing out 8192-16-byte blocks (GFx_MovieDef.h:236-276, GFx_LoadProcess.cpp:295), so the 101 extra bytes are neighbouring tags inside the same block for all but a tag landing in the last 128 bytes of a block. (b) The copy goes through safe_copy, which is SEH-guarded (src/goblin_gfx_probe.cpp:367-371) and returns false, and the caller's `if (!t || !safe_copy(...)) return false;` degrades to 'no logo', not a fault. (c) Nothing past +0x17 is ever parsed: with flags0=0x06 (HasChar|HasMatrix only) and flags1=0x10, Unpack stops after the matrix, and our 9-byte LOGO_MATRIX at +0xe ends at +0x17. Also note the clone is not an allocator hazard - the frame-element dtor calls slot 0 with rdx=0 so the tag is never freed. Two incidental errors in the finding's framing: the vanilla tag already has flags1=0x10, so our `flags1 |= 0x10` is a no-op, and the tag object is 8+12 rounded to the class layout (~27 bytes allocated), not literally 20.

title: OK-VERIFIED: resetting the single shared command list while an earlier submission is still executing is legal
claim: This looks like the classic D3D12 lifetime bug: one ID3D12GraphicsCommandList shared by all frame slots, Reset() with slot N's allocator while slot M's submission (a higher fence value) may still be running on the GPU. It is correct. Only the ALLOCATOR reset needs the GPU to be done, and that one is gated on this slot's own fence; because both submissions go on the same in-order queue, slot N's fence completing proves every earlier submission (including everything recorded from slot N's allocator) has finished.
evidence: learn.microsoft.com ID3D12GraphicsCommandList::Reset, Remarks: "By using Reset, you can re-use command list tracking structures without any allocations. Unlike ID3D12CommandAllocator::Reset, you can call ID3D12GraphicsCommandList::Reset while the command list is still being executed." and "The command allocator passed to Reset cannot be associated with any other currently-recording command list." Our list is always in the closed state at that point (Close() at overlay_d3d12.cpp:1156 after CreateCommandList, and at 1253/1262/1271/1383 on every exit after a Reset). The per-slot gate is overlay_d3d12.cpp:1236-1238 `if (slot.fence_value != 0 && impl_->fence->GetCompletedValue() < slot.fence_value) return RenderResult::Skipped;`.
recommendation: No change. Leave the existing comment; do not add a full GPU flush here.
verify_note:
CONFIRMED here means I independently reproduced the OK-VERIFIED conclusion: there is no defect.

Re-derived from the code rather than the evidence string:
- One shared list: Impl::command_list, created once at overlay_d3d12.cpp:1152-1156 from slots[0]->allocator and immediately Closed.
- The only allocator Reset is overlay_d3d12.cpp:1243, guarded by the per-slot gate at 1236-1238 (`slot.fence_value != 0 && fence->GetCompletedValue() < slot.fence_value -> Skipped`). slot.fence_value is assigned at 1394 immediately after the ExecuteCommandLists/Signal pair at 1388-1391, and the recording that produced that submission used exactly this slot's allocator, so the ID3D12CommandAllocator::Reset precondition (GPU done with every list recorded from it) is satisfied. Values come from a single monotonic counter (next_fence_value++ at 1390) signalled on one in-order queue, so completion of slot N's value also implies completion of every earlier submission - the finding's secondary argument holds, though only the allocator needs it.
- ID3D12GraphicsCommandList::Reset while a prior submission executes is explicitly permitted, and our list is never in the recording state at that point: I checked every return between the Reset at 1244 and the tail - 1253, 1262, 1271 all Close() first, and the only other exits are 1245 (Reset itself failed, nothing was opened) and 1384 (after Close at 1383). There is no path that leaves the list open across a frame.
- slot.fence_value == 0 only for a never-submitted slot; slots[0]'s allocator has one recorded-but-never-executed list from CreateCommandList, and resetting an allocator whose lists never executed is legal.

title: OK-VERIFIED: the row-looking projection matrix fed to mul(ProjectionMatrix, pos) is correct under HLSL's default cbuffer packing
claim: The 16 floats are laid out so that the translation sits in the last four (as rows), while the shader computes mul(M, v) - which, read as row-major, would drop the translation into w and produce garbage clip coordinates. It is right: fxc packs a cbuffer float4x4 column-major by default, and the code compiles with no D3DCOMPILE_PACK_MATRIX_ROW_MAJOR, so M[i][j] reads data[j*4+i] and out.x = 2/(R-L)*x + (R+L)/(L-R), out.w = 1. This is byte-for-byte the imgui_impl_dx12 matrix and shader pairing.
evidence: overlay_d3d12.cpp:160 `output.pos = mul(ProjectionMatrix, float4(input.pos.xy, 0.0f, 1.0f));`; overlay_d3d12.cpp:937-943 the matrix; overlay_d3d12.cpp:118-119 the only compile flags are `D3DCOMPILE_ENABLE_STRICTNESS | D3DCOMPILE_OPTIMIZATION_LEVEL3` (no row-major packing flag). Root constant count matches the cbuffer: 4x4 + uint + float + float2 = 20 dwords, declared as Num32BitValues = 20 at overlay_d3d12.cpp:330 and uploaded as SetGraphicsRoot32BitConstants(0, 20, &constants, 0) at 951-952, with static_assert(sizeof(RootConstants) == 20u * sizeof(uint32_t)) at 315.
recommendation: No change. If anyone ever adds D3DCOMPILE_PACK_MATRIX_ROW_MAJOR to compile_shader, the matrix must be transposed at the same time.
verify_note:
CONFIRMED here means I independently reproduced the OK-VERIFIED conclusion: the code is right.

Verified in-file: no matrix packing flag is passed to D3DCompile (overlay_d3d12.cpp:118-119 is exactly D3DCOMPILE_ENABLE_STRICTNESS | D3DCOMPILE_OPTIMIZATION_LEVEL3), so fxc's default column_major cbuffer packing applies. Under that packing data[0..3] is column 0 and data[12..15] is column 3, so with the matrix at 937-943 the shader's mul(ProjectionMatrix, float4(pos,0,1)) at line 160 yields out.x = 2/(R-L)*x + (R+L)/(L-R), out.y = 2/(T-B)*y + (T+B)/(B-T), out.z = 0.5, out.w = 1 - correct clip coordinates, and byte-identical to the imgui_impl_dx12 matrix/shader pairing (same 0.5 in m22/m23 and same trailing row).

Root-constant plumbing also checks out and is self-consistent: 16 floats + uint + float + float2 = 20 dwords; Num32BitValues = 20 (line 330), static_assert(sizeof(RootConstants) == 20 * sizeof(uint32_t)) (line 315), SetGraphicsRoot32BitConstants(0, 20, &constants, 0) (951-952) with Dest offset 0. Root 32-bit constants use the same cbuffer layout rules, so the packing argument applies unchanged.

title: OK-VERIFIED: the "our retained backbuffer refs make the game's ResizeBuffers fail safely" strategy also holds under Proton
claim: before_resize_impl deliberately returns false and keeps the live backbuffer references when it cannot prove the GPU is idle, relying on DXGI to reject the resize ("Keep the live references so the downstream resize fails safely"). That relies on an enforcement the docs require but that a reimplementation could skip - and if it were skipped, after_resize's !resources_released branch permanently quarantines the session and leaks it (overlay_present.cpp:1585-1595). Checked: Wine's D3D12 swapchain enforces it, so the strategy is sound on Proton as well as Windows.
evidence: learn.microsoft.com IDXGISwapChain::ResizeBuffers, Remarks: "You can't resize a swap chain unless you release all outstanding references to its back buffers... Indirect references are held by views to a resource, ... a command list that used the resource..." (which is also why overlay_d3d12.cpp:684 resets command_list inside release_backbuffer_state - correct). Wine dlls/dxgi/swapchain.c d3d12_swapchain_ResizeBuffers: `ID3D12Resource_AddRef(swapchain->buffers[i]); if ((refcount = ID3D12Resource_Release(swapchain->buffers[i]))) { WARN("Buffer %p has %lu references left.\n", ...); return DXGI_ERROR_INVALID_CALL; }` - it fails the call rather than resizing under us. Also verified from the SetFullscreenState docs that a fullscreen transition cannot invalidate our buffers behind our back: "For the flip presentation model, after you transition the display state to full screen, you must call ResizeBuffers to ensure that your call to IDXGISwapChain1::Present1 succeeds" - so the not-hooked SetFullscreenState (vtable slot 10) is always followed by a ResizeBuffers we do intercept.
recommendation: No change. Worth keeping the Wine citation next to the comment at overlay_present.cpp:1535 so the next reader does not re-litigate the Proton case.
verify_note:
CONFIRMED here means I agree there is no defect - but note that the Wine source quote is neither reproducible in this sandbox nor necessary for the conclusion.

What I verified in our code:
- Session::before_resize (overlay_d3d12.cpp:1399-1458) returns false on every path where GPU completion is unproven (SetEventOnCompletion failure 1413-1422, 2000 ms budget exhausted 1428-1432, WAIT_FAILED 1447-1451, unexpected wait result 1452-1456) and retains all backbuffer references; it only releases state when the device is confirmed removed (1414-1418) or the fence proved completion.
- before_resize_impl (overlay_present.cpp:1528-1546) then re-installs the retained session as g_session (1536) with the comment at 1535 and reports resources_released == false.
- release_backbuffer_state does reset command_list first (overlay_d3d12.cpp:684), which is the indirect-reference case the ResizeBuffers docs call out.
- SetFullscreenState (IDXGISwapChain slot 10) is indeed not shadowed: the only shadowed slots are 8, 13, 22, 38, 39 (overlay_dxgi_shadow.cpp:32-36, 489-513).

Why the Wine question is not load-bearing: the strategy does not actually depend on the runtime enforcing the reference rule. If a non-conforming implementation resizes anyway, after_resize's !resources_released branch (overlay_present.cpp:1585-1595) releases ownership of the unfenced session (deliberate leak), clears rebuild/retry, sets g_renderer_healthy=false and logs. That is fail-closed: no rendering happens against buffers we cannot prove are ours. So the code is safe on both a conforming and a non-conforming DXGI, and the Proton-specific claim is unnecessary. I could not re-derive the Wine dlls/dxgi/swapchain.c quote - there is no Wine tree in the sandbox and I did not fetch one - so treat that specific sentence as unverified rather than established.
corrected: No defect, but the finding's justification is stronger than needed and partly unverifiable here: correctness does not rest on Wine/DXGI enforcing the outstanding-reference rule, because after_resize:1585-1595 already fails closed if a resize succeeds under us. The Wine source quote was not independently reproduced.
